groups.title: Verbstem structure and unified meaning
groups.writingJob: Keep a monomorphemic or polymorphemic verbstem as one lexical predicate, preserve its internal morph boundaries, and never block the stem merely because an internal morph lacks an individual gloss.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recognize internal morph boundaries while reading the verbstem and its translation as one meaningful whole.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies a whole or analyzed stem; the application preserves the typed internal structure and treats the complete stem as the lexical unit.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add an internal-morph or gloss control. Typed hyphens remain internal boundaries, not separate stem slots.
groups.userChoiceJob: The user may type a whole or internally analyzed verbstem.
groups.applicationJob: The application preserves one verbstem, its internal morph boundaries, and its unified lexical meaning.
groups.derivedCueJob: The Formula and Diagram identify verbstem morphs and their internal boundaries.
groups.proposal: Preserve one verbstem with its real internal boundaries and unified meaning, even when an internal morph's separate meaning is unknown.

groups.title: Verb citation and Valence
groups.writingJob: Represent a cited verb as a verbcore whose Valence states the required intransitive, projective, reflexive, or reciprocal object relationship.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to recover a verb's required object relationship from its citation form instead of treating the stem as valence-free.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended verb and object relationship when it is not already known; the application builds the matching citation structure and contextual carriers.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Valence and object meaning controls. Do not expose citation prefixes or zero carriers as raw choices.
groups.userChoiceJob: The user chooses Valence or object meaning only when the source does not already determine it.
groups.applicationJob: The application builds and preserves the required verbcore citation structure.
groups.derivedCueJob: The Formula and Diagram identify the object relationship, Valence carriers, and verbstem separately.
groups.proposal: Make every verb citation preserve its required Valence while keeping the exact carrier realization automatic.

groups.title: Basis of verbstem class
groups.writingJob: Assign Class A, B, C, or D by the relation between the imperfective and perfective stem, especially the treatment of the imperfective stem's final vowel.
groups.readingJob: Explain that verbstem class names a real stem alternation rather than a spelling label.
groups.decisionSplit: A built-in stem supplies its lexical class automatically; the user supplies the class for an unknown stem when the grammar cannot predict it; the application uses the class to form the stem.
groups.controlPolicy: Keep the existing Stem class control available for unknown input, but do not ask for class when the selected built-in stem already determines it.
groups.userChoiceJob: The user supplies stem class only for genuinely unknown input whose class the grammar cannot determine.
groups.applicationJob: The application uses a known or supplied class to control the imperfective-perfective relation.
groups.derivedCueJob: The Formula and Diagram identify the active class and aspect on the realized verbstem.
groups.proposal: Use the stem's licensed class to control its imperfective-perfective relation and show that automatic work as a formula cue.

groups.title: Perfective forms of Classes A-D
groups.writingJob: Form the licensed Class A, B, C, or D perfective stem, including deletion, replacement, addition, and silently present causative structure.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover the perfective operation and distinguish phonologically identical Class B outcomes with different morphology.
groups.decisionSplit: The stem class and lexical record determine the perfective operation; the application performs it.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add deletion, glottal-stop, or silent-carrier controls.
groups.proposal: Make each verbstem class produce its exact perfective stem automatically.

groups.title: Conditioned imperfective stem shapes
groups.writingJob: Choose the licensed imperfective shape from class, mood, tense, number, and the following morphs.
groups.readingJob: Show why one lexical imperfective stem may appear in one, two, or four surface shapes.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses genuine mood, tense, and subject number; the application selects the conditioned stem shape.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a short, long, or truncated stem-shape control.
groups.proposal: Make imperfective stem shape an automatic consequence of the grammatical environment.

groups.title: Class B spelling and sound changes
groups.writingJob: Apply every Class B final-vowel loss, spelling change, and resulting sound change through the ordinary Lesson 2 spelling path.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover the underlying stem and avoid misclassifying traditional oa and ia spellings as Class C.
groups.decisionSplit: The class operation triggers the change; the application spells and realizes it automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add spelling or sound-change controls.
groups.proposal: Send every Class B perfective through the common spelling and sound system.

groups.title: Licensed variable class membership
groups.writingJob: Preserve licensed Class A and Class B perfective alternatives for variable stems without turning evidence absence into no form.
groups.readingJob: Show both licensed class analyses and their perfective results.
groups.decisionSplit: The user may choose between genuinely licensed class alternatives; the application blocks unlicensed classes.
groups.controlPolicy: Filter the Stem class control to the licensed alternatives.
groups.proposal: Offer only genuine variable-class alternatives and generate the matching perfective.

groups.title: Class guidelines 1-4
groups.writingJob: Apply the general class guidelines for monosyllables, final consonant clusters, final ka, and final tla while preserving stated exceptions and alternatives.
groups.readingJob: Present the guidelines as useful grammar, not as a claim that every perfective is predictable.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives class where a rule determines it and asks for a class only where the source remains genuinely open.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not replace lexical class knowledge with blind shape guessing.
groups.proposal: Use the first four class guidelines wherever they truly determine or limit class.

groups.title: Class guidelines 5-8
groups.writingJob: Apply the change-of-state hua, ya, final o, and listed Class D guidelines with every licensed alternative and exception.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader connect semantic and final-shape conditions to the resulting class.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives a determined class and preserves real alternatives; the user resolves only a genuinely open class choice.
groups.controlPolicy: Keep semantic and lexical conditions automatic where known.
groups.proposal: Use the remaining class guidelines as grammar rules rather than example whitelists.

groups.title: Stem class cooperation with tense
groups.writingJob: Select the exact stem shape and tense carrier for every Class A-D mood-tense cell.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through the predicate tables by class, aspect, mood, tense, and stem shape.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses genuine mood and tense; the application selects aspect, stem shape, and tense carrier.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose table cells, aspect, or allomorphs as extra choices.
groups.proposal: Make the Lesson 7 predicate tables the automatic finite-formation path.

groups.title: Analysis and translation of complete VNCs
groups.writingJob: Build a complete VNC with the obligatory Subject-Predicate division and preserve the exact class-conditioned predicate.
groups.readingJob: Guide linear and diagrammatic reading while preserving genuine ambiguities and the difference between carrier, content, function, and translation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies grammatical choices; the application builds the complete VNC and both explanatory projections.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not make analysis format or translation wording authorize grammar.
groups.proposal: Use the canonical Result for both linear and diagrammatic Lesson 7 analysis.

groups.title: Object relationship contrasts
groups.writingJob: Preserve distinct human/nonhuman projective, reflexive, and plural reciprocal readings and their exact valence structures.
groups.readingJob: Use subject and object context to distinguish singular reflexive from plural reflexive or reciprocal meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuine object relationship and referent; the application enforces its person, number, and humanness conditions.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer reciprocal meaning for singular subjects or collapse human and nonhuman object roles.
groups.proposal: Keep every Lesson 7 object relationship distinct in grammar and interpretation.

groups.title: Adverb plus tla fusion
groups.writingJob: Distinguish an unfused transitive tla object from a licensed adverb-plus-tla derived intransitive stem and carry the selected structure into the Result.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recognize when tla belongs inside a derived stem rather than occupying the object position.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies or selects the intended source structure; the application enforces the fusion and resulting valence.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse typed Stem or Embed plus matrix structure; do not add a raw fusion-spelling control.
groups.proposal: Make tla fusion a typed derivational structure with a distinct intransitive Result.
